chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Barqī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Allah is more generous than to burden the people with what they cannot bear, and Allah is mightier than that there should be in His dominion what He does not will.

key_terms.أَعَزُّ: mightier and more exalted in power
key_terms.أَكْرَمُ: more generous and noble in dealing with His creation
key_terms.سُلْطَانِهِ: His dominion, authority, and sovereign power
key_terms.يُطِيقُونَ: they are able to bear or endure
key_terms.يُكَلِّفَ: to impose duty or religious responsibility

ai.seo_question: Does Allah burden people beyond their ability, or does anything happen outside His will?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms two theological principles: Allah does not impose obligations beyond human capacity, and nothing occurs within His dominion outside His will. It expresses divine justice and divine sovereignty together in a concise creedal formulation.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Barqy, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more Benevolent than for Him<sup>azwj</sup> to Encumber the people what they are not enduring; and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Mightier than that there would happen to be in His<sup>azwj</sup> Authority what He<sup>azwj</sup> does not want’.
